newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss current account surplus widens in 1995.
newsitem.headline: Swiss current account surplus widens in 1995.

text.p: Switzerland's 1995 current account balance of payments surplus rose to 25.0 billion from a revised 24.4 billion in 1994 as growing net investment income more than compensated for a declining trade surplus, the Swiss National Bank (SNB) said on Tuesday.
Net investment income rose 3.1 billion to 20.8 billion, while the trade surplus slipped to 1.8 billion from 3.2 billion.
Net receipts from services continued their downward trend, slipping to 14.9 billion from 16.1 billion.
Capital flows between Switzerland and foreign countries contracted sharply, but the decline reflected primarily short-term flows.
Direct investment abroad eased to 14.0 billion from the record 14.8 billion in 1994, while foreign direct investment in Switzerland fell by half to 2.3 billion.

Portfolio investment abroad slumped to 11.0 billion from 26.1 billion, while portfolio investment in Switzerland jumped to 5.9 billion from 1.2 billion. The increased flow went almost exclusively into shares.
The deficit in the balance of payments financial account, excluding the central bank but including net errors and omissions, widened to 25.0 billion from a revised 22.8 billion shortfall.
Currency reserves at the SNB fell by 3.7 billion, reflecting exchange rate movements.
